## Updates on Transparency, Participation, and Collaboration

**September 27, 2024** - The National Archives releases its [Open Government Plan](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/open-government-plan-6.0.pdf) for 2025-2027. The public can send their feedback to [opengov@nara.gov](mailto:opengov@nara.gov).

**August 5, 2024 -** The U.S. Open Government Secretariat publishes the [mid-term self-assessment](https://www.gsa.gov/usopengov) of the United States’ 5th Open Government National Action Plan.

**July 12, 2024** \- NARA requests public suggestions for its upcoming Open Government plan. Please send your comments and ideas that will help us increase participation, collaboration, and transparency to [opengov@nara.gov](mailto:opengov@nara.gov) by July 31, 2024. [Read more in our NARAtions blog](https://narations.blogs.archives.gov/2024/07/12/have-your-say-provide-input-and-suggestions-for-naras-2025-2027-open-government-plan/).

**March 14, 2024**\- Celebrating access to public information, NARA hosts a [Sunshine Week panel](https://www.archives.gov/press/press-releases/2024/nr24-17) discussion on “Artificial Intelligence: The Intersection of Public Access and Open Government'' with Pamela Wright, Chief Innovation Officer at NARA, moderating. The panel includes Gulam Shakir, NARA’s Chief Data Officer; Abigail Potter, Senior Innovation Specialist at the Library of Congress Digital Innovation Lab; Eric Stein, Deputy Assistant Secretary for the Office of Global Information Services at the U.S. Department of State; and Bobak Talebian, Director of the Office of Information Policy of the U.S. Department of Justice. Jay Bosanko, Deputy Archivist of the United States, and Alina Semo, Director of [OGIS](https://www.archives.gov/ogis), provide opening remarks.

**January 22, 2024** \- NARA’s status updates to our commitments in the U.S. National Action Plan are published on [GSA’s Commitment Tracker](https://www.gsa.gov/usopengov).

**September 26, 2023** \- NARA publishes [Lessons Learned from the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Advisory Committee](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/lessons-learned-foia-advisory-committee.pdf). One of eight initiatives in the National Archives and Records Administration’s Fifth National Action Plan for Open Government calls on the agency to provide “lessons learned” from the creation and administration of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Advisory Committee. This document contains those learned lessons and provides ideas for consideration as NARA continues working with civil society partners to lead the U.S. on open government issues.

**August 16, 2023**\- The National Archives presents progress updates on commitments to [expand access to the National Archives, including for underserved communities](https://www.gsa.gov/usopengov), by improving the Catalog, updating Archives.gov, and engaging underserved communities at an [Open Government public engagement session on "Improving Access to Government Data, Research, and Information"](https://www.gsa.gov/usopengov) with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, the White House Council on Environmental Quality, and the General Services Administration.

**July 27, 2023** \- The National Archives posts [progress updates on the agency's commitment to Expand Online Access to the National Archives](https://www.gsa.gov/usopengov) on the Fifth U.S. Open Government [National Action Plan Commitment Tracker](https://www.gsa.gov/usopengov).

**December 7, 2022 -** The National Archives releases its [Open Government Plan for](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/2022-24-nara-nap.pdf) [2022-2024](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/2022-24-nara-nap.pdf) and provides these initiatives as recommendations for the Biden administration’s 5th Open Government U.S. National Action Plan (NAP). We will continue to follow the Administration's lead for Open Government work over the 2022-2024 timeline for this plan. The public may provide feedback to [opengov@nara.gov](mailto:opengov@nara.gov).

**November 16, 2022** - Pamela Wright, Chief Innovation Officer, received a Distinguished Executive Presidential Rank Award (PRA). Learn more in the [NARA press release](https://www.archives.gov/press/press-releases/2023/nr23-08).

**September 6, 2016 -** The National Archives releases its [Open Government Plan for 2016-2018](https://usnationalarchives.github.io/opengovplan/). This plan is made available for the first time on GitHub so the public can add issues or submit edits. The public can also send their feedback to [opengov@nara.gov](mailto:opengov@nara.gov). Learn more about the plan on the [AOTUS Blog](https://aotus.blogs.archives.gov/2016/09/06/we-want-to-hear-from-you-naras-open-government-plan-2016-2018/).

![Open Government Plan 2016-18](https://www.archives.gov/files/cui/registry/open-2016-m.jpg)

**March 29, 2016 -** The National Archives will host a webinar on Open Government from 2 - 3 p.m. to seek suggestions from the public on what to include in the agency's fourth Open Government Plan.  [Register for the webinar](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/webinar-open-government-at-the-national-archives-registration-23818937082).

**March 15, 2016 -** The National Archives kicks off the development of its fourth Open Government Plan. Check out the NARAtions Blog post, " [Share your ideas for our next Open Government Plan](https://narations.blogs.archives.gov/2016/03/15/share-your-ideas-for-our-next-open-government-plan/)." And share your ideas on the [Open Government Space on History Hub](https://historyhub.history.gov/community/open-government) or email [opengov@nara.gov](mailto:opengov@nara.gov).

**March 15, 2016 -**The National Archives launches the development of its fourth Open Government Plan. Check out the NARAtions Blog post, " [Share your ideas for our next Open Government Plan](https://narations.blogs.archives.gov/2016/03/15/share-your-ideas-for-our-next-open-government-plan/)." And share your ideas on the  [Open Government Space on History Hub](https://historyhub.history.gov/community/open-government) or email [opengov@nara.gov](mailto:opengov@nara.gov).

**March 15, 2016 -** The Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) at NARA hosts an event celebrating Sunshine Week.  Learn more about the event on the  [FOIA Ombudsman blog](http://foia.blogs.archives.gov/2016/03/16/ogis-celebrate-sunshine-week-2016/) and watch the event video.

**January 13, 2016 -** NARA launches a new pilot project from the Office of Innovation called the History Hub. This collaboration network explores new ways of connecting with and serving customers interested in historical topics related to the holdings of the National Archives. Visit the  [AOTUS Blog](http://aotus.blogs.archives.gov/2016/01/13/launch-and-learn-our-new-history-hub-pilot-project/) to learn more and the  [History Hub](https://historyhub.history.gov/welcome) to participate.

**December 2015 -** Sheryl J. Shenberger, Director of the National Declassification Center, is named as a Meritorious Executive Presidential Rank Award recipient. Learn more on the  [AOTUS blog](http://aotus.blogs.archives.gov/2016/01/07/releasing-all-we-can-protecting-what-we-must-3/).

**October 29, 2015 -** The Archivist of the United States, David Ferriero, blogs about the third Open Government National Action Plan and describes NARA's commitments to strengthen open government. Learn more on the  [AOTUS Blog](http://aotus.blogs.archives.gov/2015/10/29/national-action-plan-3-0/).

[![NARA Open Government Plan 2015](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/images/open-government-2015-th.jpg)](https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/sites/default/files/microsites/ostp/final_us_open_government_national_action_plan_3_0.pdf)**October 27, 2015 -** The United States releases the third Open Government National Action Plan.  Access the plan in  [PDF](https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/sites/default/files/microsites/ostp/final_us_open_government_national_action_plan_3_0.pdf) and learn more about the plan on the  [White House blog](https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/blog/2015/10/27/advancing-open-and-citizen-centered-government).

[![Wikiconference USA](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/images/wikicon-2015.jpg)](http://aotus.blogs.archives.gov/2015/10/02/national-archives-hosts-wikiconference-usa/)**October 9-11, 2015 -** NARA is a co-organizer and host site of WikiConference USA, the annual national conference of Wikimedia enthusiasts and volunteers in the U.S. Learn more on the [AOTUS blog](http://aotus.blogs.archives.gov/2015/10/02/national-archives-hosts-wikiconference-usa/).

**July 21, 2015 -** NARA announces participation in a FOIA pilot to test the feasibility of posting online FOIA responses so that they are not just available to the individual requester, but to the general public as well. Learn more on the [NARAtions Blog](http://narations.blogs.archives.gov/2015/07/21/nara-participation-in-new-foia-pilot/).

**April 2015 -** NARA publishes its [Plain Writing Compliance Report for 2014](https://www.archives.gov/open/plain-writing/reports/). Learn more about [NARA's plain writing efforts and previous reports](https://www.archives.gov/open/plain-writing/).

[![NARA Open Government Plan for 2014-2016](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/images/open-government-plan-3-th.jpg)](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/open-government-plan-3.0.pdf)**May 30, 2014 -** NARA publishes its third Open Government Plan for 2014-2016. Access the plan in [PDF](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/open-government-plan-3.0.pdf) and [Word](https://www.archives.gov/open/open-government-plan-3.0.docx) versions and view NARA's [previous Open Government Plans](https://www.archives.gov/open/open-plan.html).

**April 2014 -** NARA publishes its [Plain Writing Compliance Report for 2013](https://www.archives.gov/files/open/plain-writing/reports/compliance-report-0414.pdf). Learn more about NARA's plain writing efforts and previous reports on [Archives.gov/open/plain-writing](https://www.archives.gov/open/plain-writing/).

**April 2, 2014 -** The NDC Blog seeks public suggestions for what should be included in the National Archives and Records Administration's third open government plan, with an emphasis on declassification topics.  Read more on the  [NDC blog](http://blogs.archives.gov/ndc/2014/04/02/the-ndc-and-open-government/).

**April 2, 2014 -** The National Archives seeks public feedback on the development of the agency's third Open Government Plan.  Read about this and comment on the NARAtions blog post, " [Have Your Say: Open Government at the Archives!](http://blogs.archives.gov/online-public-access/?p=9226)" or send your suggestions to  [webprogram@nara.gov](mailto:webprogram@nara.gov).

**February 12, 2014 -** The National Historical Publications and Records Commission (NHPRC) seeks public feedback on proposed changes to the grants program.  Read more about it on the  [Annotations Blog](http://blogs.archives.gov/nhprc/2014/02/13/overview-of-proposed-changes-to-the-nhprc-grants-program/).

**March 10, 2014 -** The National Declassification Center celebrates the completion of a quality assurance review of over 351 million pages of historically valuable classified records.  Learn more about this effort on [the NDC blog](http://blogs.archives.gov/ndc/2014/03/10/the-ndc-celebrates-success/).

**March 10, 2014 -** The National Declassification Center celebrates the completion of a quality assurance review of over 351 million pages of historically valuable classified records.  Learn more about this effort on [the NDC blog](http://blogs.archives.gov/ndc/2014/03/10/the-ndc-celebrates-success/).

**March 6, 2014 -** The Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) discusses Sunshine Week events in the blog post, " [A Sunny Forecast](http://blogs.archives.gov/foiablog/2014/03/06/a-sunny-forecast/)."
